clue.text: One next to bay five picked up nuts and bolts

indicators.note: picked up as a listener picks up speech, so the phrase is heard rather than read

parts.note: in a row of numbered loading bays, the one beside bay five is bay six

explanation.surface: A warehouse worker collects some hardware fittings from the bay beside bay five.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nuts and bolts' looks like the thing picked up, but it is the definition; 'picked up' signals that BAY SIX is spoken aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: The nuts and bolts of something are its fundamental practical details, its essentials.

clue.text: Babe's smashed everything in this sport

indicators.note: smashed into pieces, the letters are rearranged

parts.note: all means everything

explanation.surface: Babe Ruth broke every record in this sport.
explanation.walkthrough: Babe Ruth was the most famous American baseball player, which makes the clue nearly self-describing.
explanation.definitionFit: The sport Babe Ruth played is the American bat-and-ball game with bases.

clue.text: Sugar, maybe, fed to group — that fills a gap

indicators.note: one thing fed to another goes inside it

parts.note: a set is a group
Alan Sugar is a British businessman, host of the UK Apprentice, so Sugar is an example surname for Alan

explanation.surface: Sugar is fed to a group of people to fill a gap in their diet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sugar' looks like food; it is Lord Alan Sugar, the British tycoon who hosts the UK version of The Apprentice.
explanation.definitionFit: A sealant is a substance such as mastic used to plug cracks and joints.

clue.text: Sign of company, with navy south of island

indicators.note: in a down answer, south of means below, so these pieces follow the island

parts.note: Capri is an Italian island
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: A sign for a company whose navy is stationed south of an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Capricorn is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac, the goat.

clue.text: Cadet in conflict with our teacher

indicators.note: letters in conflict are at odds and jumbled, so the two words are rearranged together

explanation.surface: A military cadet is at loggerheads with the class teacher.
explanation.definitionFit: A teacher is someone whose job is instructing others, a schooling professional.

clue.text: Enjoyed daft mug shot in divine accounting event

indicators.note: something shot is ruined or broken, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A grinning mugshot taken at heaven's audit.
explanation.definitionFit: On Judgement Day God is believed to call everyone to account for their lives.

clue.text: One indicating ratio of emigrant group without base

indicators.note: in a down answer the base of a word is its last letter, which is dropped

parts.note: a colony is a group of settlers who emigrated

explanation.surface: A statistician measures the ratio of a settler group that has no home base.
explanation.definitionFit: A colon is the punctuation mark used in writing ratios such as 3:1.

clue.text: In casual footwear, the Queen goes to north land

indicators.note: in a down answer north is upward, so these letters move higher up the word

parts.note: a trainer is a sports shoe worn casually
ER is Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: Wearing trainers, the Queen heads north to her lands.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'north' is up the column, so 'goes to north' lifts the Queen's letters from the bottom of the footwear to near its top.
explanation.definitionFit: Terrain means land, especially regarding its physical features.

clue.text: Early locomotive leaves

definitions.meaning: Stephenson's ... was a pioneering steam engine of 1829
..., also called arugula, is a peppery salad leaf

explanation.surface: An old steam engine departs from the station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' looks like a verb, departs; it is the salad plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Stephenson's famous engine and the salad green rucola share this name.

clue.text: Burger that's 25p?

parts.note: 25p is a quarter of a British pound, so a burger of that value is jokingly named after the fast-food size

explanation.surface: A very cheap burger at a snack bar.
explanation.walkthrough: The fast-food burger is named for a quarter pound of beef; the clue reads pound as money.
explanation.definitionFit: The fast-food item is a large burger whose patty weighs four ounces before cooking.

clue.text: Tax shelter protecting a politician in France of the time

indicators.note: a shelter protecting something has it inside, so the other pieces go within the sty

parts.note: a sty is a shelter for pigs
MP is Member of Parliament
du is French for 'of the'

explanation.surface: A pig shed shields a French MP from the taxes of the day.
explanation.walkthrough: Stamp duty is a British tax paid on buying property; 'in France' tells you to read 'of the' in French.
explanation.definitionFit: Stamp duty is a levy charged by government on documents and property purchases.

clue.text: Addition to music player disco regularly used

indicators.note: only every other letter of the two words is used, taken at regular intervals

explanation.surface: Something extra fitted to a record player at a disco.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the 2nd, 4th and so on letters: pLaYeR dIsCo.
explanation.definitionFit: Lyrics are the words set to a tune, added to the melody to make a song.

clue.text: Start to blanche more nuts without opening heated container

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter
the opening of a word is its first letter, which is dropped here

parts.note: nuts means crazy, so more nuts is crazier

explanation.surface: A cook blanches ever-wilder nuts, but the container is never opened.
explanation.definitionFit: A brazier is a metal pan or stand holding burning coals, a container for heat.

clue.text: Herald from distant Spain after lover

indicators.note: the distant-Spain part comes after the lover part in the answer

parts.note: a fan is a lover or devotee of something
distant means far
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: A messenger arrives from far-off Spain, following a sweetheart.
explanation.definitionFit: A fanfare is a flourish of trumpets announcing an arrival, so it heralds.

clue.text: Learner very exuberant over game

parts.note: L is the learner driver's plate
OTT is over the top, wildly excessive
O is over in cricket scoring

explanation.surface: A beginner gets overexcited about a game.
explanation.definitionFit: Lotto is a lottery-style game of chance, also a form of bingo.

clue.text: Breaking out innocent revolutionary with little noise

indicators.note: a revolution turns something round, so this word is read backwards

parts.note: innocent means pure
a ting is a small ringing sound

explanation.surface: An innocent revolutionary escapes quietly from prison.
explanation.definitionFit: A volcano breaking out is erupting; spots on skin also erupt.

clue.text: Old volunteers watch out carrying large dishes etc

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, the British volunteer reserve, now renamed

indicators.note: something carrying another holds it within

parts.note: beware means watch out
L is the size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Former volunteers are warned to be careful while carrying big plates.
explanation.definitionFit: Tableware covers the plates, cutlery and glasses used for dining.

clue.text: Outline is horse climbing in sunless void

indicators.note: the reversed letters sit inside the outer pair
a void word is emptied of its middle, leaving its outer letters
in a down answer climbing reads upward, so these letters are reversed

parts.note: a pony is a small horse

explanation.surface: A sketch shows a horse climbing in a sunless void.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' reverses IS PONY into YNOPSI; 'void' leaves S and S from 'sunless'.
explanation.definitionFit: A synopsis is a brief summary giving the outline of a story.

clue.text: Obtain dram on vacation enjoying Canadian city

parts.note: to win is to obtain
a nip is a small drink, a dram

indicators.note: a word on vacation is emptied of its middle, leaving only its outside letters

explanation.surface: A holidaymaker gets a whisky while enjoying a Canadian city.
explanation.definitionFit: Winnipeg is the capital of the province of Manitoba.

clue.text: Reportedly where Colossus overlooked harbour raids

indicators.note: something reported is passed on in speech, so the phrase is heard aloud

parts.note: the Colossus of Rhodes was a giant statue at the harbour of Rhodes, so this is in Rhodes

explanation.surface: A history note on harbour raids where the Colossus once stood.
explanation.definitionFit: Inroads are hostile incursions into territory, attacks or raids.

clue.text: Flexible times to secure result

indicators.note: to secure something is to hold it fast within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: by means times, as in 'three by four'
an end is a result or outcome

explanation.surface: Flexible working hours help get results.
explanation.definitionFit: Bendy describes something pliable that can be bent easily.

clue.text: New treats prepared for rabbits

indicators.note: a dish prepared is made up afresh, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Fresh treats have been made ready for pet bunnies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rabbits' looks like the animals; it is the verb meaning chatter on, as in rabbiting on.
explanation.definitionFit: To rabbit on is British slang for talking at length, chattering.

clue.text: Goodness in school's roast

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: SCH is the abbreviation for school
cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like goodness

explanation.surface: Goodness, the school dinner roast!
explanation.definitionFit: To scorch is to burn the surface, to roast fiercely.

clue.text: Reindeer around ridge, four overlooking edges

parts.note: ca, short for circa, means around
a rib is a raised ridge

indicators.note: the outside letters of the word are ignored, keeping only its middle

explanation.surface: A reindeer goes round a mountain ridge, four of them watching from the rim.
explanation.definitionFit: Caribou is the North American name for the same deer species as the reindeer.

clue.text: Wash black article after another

indicators.note: the second article comes after the first in the answer

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
another article here is the, the definite one

explanation.surface: Wash the black items one after another.
explanation.definitionFit: To bathe is to wash, in a bath or by immersion.

clue.text: Ace graduate redesigned store

parts.note: MA is a Master of Arts, a graduate

indicators.note: a redesigned word has had its letters laid out afresh

explanation.surface: A graduate has given a shop a makeover.
explanation.definitionFit: A maestro is an expert or virtuoso, someone who is an ace at something.

clue.text: Respond about facts lacking in case

parts.note: re means about, concerning

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outer letters, which are taken away

explanation.surface: A lawyer replies on the facts missing from the case.
explanation.definitionFit: To react is to respond to a stimulus or event.

clue.text: Grease smeared on greyish brown garment

indicators.note: in an across answer one piece sits on, or follows, the other

parts.note: dun is a dull greyish-brown colour

indicators.note: grease smeared about is spread around, so its letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A mechanic gets grease all over brown work clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Dungarees are overalls, trousers with a bib and braces, a work garment.

clue.text: Drunk shortly embracing English boozer

indicators.note: the jumbled letters wrap around the extra letter
drunk letters reel about and are jumbled

explanation.surface: A tipsy man soon hugs an English drinker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunk' turns SHORTLY into HOSTLRY; 'embracing' puts E inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A boozer is British slang for a pub, and a hostelry is an inn or pub.

clue.text: Against Hoovers using bags

indicators.note: to bag is to hold inside, so the run of letters is held within the words

explanation.surface: An objection to vacuum cleaners that use bags.
explanation.definitionFit: Versus is Latin for against, as in one team playing another.
